..
Issued at 123 AM CST Thu Nov 26 2026

Early Thanksgiving morning GOES-19 water vapor and regional 
mosaic imagery depict a meteorologically interesting scene with 
a pair of upper-level waves in the process of phasing over the 
eastern United States. The primary wave continues to drive an 
area of warm-air advection snow along the Missouri/Illinois 
border, while the secondary wave over Florida is supporting the
rapid deepening of a surface low pressure system off the South 
Carolina coast. Amidst all the active weather ongoing across the
country at press time, all is quiet on the homefront so far as 
we remain safely on the dry southern side of a surface high 
pressure system extending westward over the Great Lakes. 

The forecast for today and tomorrow appears to be in good shape
with minimal changes needed to the gridded database. Generally 
speaking, the surface low is expected to lift northward through
the next 24 hours more or less along the Appalachian Mountains 
reaching northern New York by Friday evening. As this occurs, 
the northwestern edge of the precipitation shield along the 
backside of the mature cyclone will reach across the Great 
Lakes, leading to steady rain spreading across our area today. 
We continue to favor rain arriving during the afternoon and 
evening hours and then tapering Friday morning. There remains 
variance in the northwestern edge of the rain shield in guidance
even at this hour, so maintained a gradient in PoPs (ranging 
from near 30% at Rockford to 100% in northwestern Indiana). 
Suppose a snowflake or two may mix in by Friday morning, though 
warm ambient air and ground temperatures will prevent anything 
from sticking. 

The bigger story with this storm system for us will be blustery
winds with BUFKIT mixing profiles continuing to support gusts 
of 30 to locally 40 mph at times this afternoon (out of the 
northeast) through Friday morning (out of the northwest). Did 
make note of a small clustering of ensemble low paths that are 
slightly deeper and further to the west than ensemble means, 
which hint at a play for gusts to ramp up to 45-50 mph 
particularly this evening (The 00Z HRRR is reflective of such an
outcome). Don't see that evolution as particularly likely at 
this point, but it is still worth mentioning.

After rain tapers Friday, some thinning of cloud cover and low-
level warm air advection (from the northwest) beneath a short-
wavelength ridge will encourage highs to bounce back to the mid 
40s. 

Friday night into Saturday morning, a quickly-moving upper- 
level wave will propagate across the central Great Lakes. While 
the low-level airmass will be quite parched, relatively steep 
mid-level lapse rates driven by dynamic cooling does give pause 
for a chance for a few snow showers mainly along the Illinois 
and Wisconsin border. Did opt to introduce "silent" 10% chances
for snow with explicit mention of flurries to the forecast 
north of I-80 for this potential though will note about 50% of 
most recent ensemble membership does produce measurable 
precipitation with the wave (moreso in Wisconsin). After the 
morning system, clearing skies and another bout of low-level 
warm air advection will drive high temperatures toward the 50 
degree mark. 

Yet another storm system (currently in the north Gulf of 
Alaska) is due to move eastward through the central US on 
Sunday. Over the past 24 hours, have noted increasing 
consistency in the evolution of the system within ensemble 
guidance with a scenario of a surface low moving along the Ohio 
River gaining traction. Should this occur, our area would be in 
line for a period of steady stratiform rain on Sunday, though 
forecast soundings look precariously close to changing to snow 
across northwestern Illinois by Sunday evening. So, opted to 
lean on the in-house Bourgouin precipitation type method to 
introduce a rain/snow mix into our gridded forecast across 
interior northwestern Illinois as the system pulls away Sunday 
night. 

Looking toward next week and the start of meteorological 
winter, there remains a persistent signal for temperatures to 
trend back above average by midweek before predictability drops 
off thereafter (850mb temperature and 500mb height IQRs spread 
to 15 degrees and 30 dam respectively by the end of next week). 

Borchardt
